page.layout: One printed page, one column. Top: page number "4" at the head left, then a printed ornament. Below it, a centred heading in capitals over two lines. Then one verse paragraph in italic, opening with a large initial I. Below the text, at the right, the catchword "LAMEN-". The right margin shows only show-through from the reverse side, which is not transcribed.

p.i: IRa quum Superi Numinis auspice, Pollutas variis criminibus ferox Inuasit Solymas Rex Babylonius, Vicitque Assyrio fortior agmine: Et quum Barbarico militis impetu Gentis tunc domitæ per trepidas domos Feruens diripuit diuitias, simul Cum sanctis adytis, & penetralibus Fuso purpuream sanguine civium Urbem flammiuomis perdidit ignibus: Vates ille Deo plenus, & integer Vitæ, fœdifragis qui popularibus Euentura suis tot mala dixerat, (Quòd recto Superum tramite deuij Nollent æthereiferre iugum patris) Ardentem attonito Lumine patriam Cernens, atque Sacri Liminis atria Flammis versa simul tristibus, & suæ Urbis strata feris compita cædibus, Gentisque Abramidum reliquias sequi Vinctas Imperium, & iussa ferocia, Rupit pressa diu corde silentia Hac miscens querulis carmina fletibus.

page.notes: The initial I is a large woodcut-style capital, joined to the first word as "IRa". The verse runs as one continuous paragraph with no stanza breaks on the scan. The printed line "Nollent æthereiferre" is run together in print; I left the spacing as it appears on the scan, with the word "æthereiferre" unbroken. The first line of the heading is hyphenated at the line end as "LA-", which I kept. Printed "ARGVMENTVM" is written with U as the capital vowel. Some letters in the italic verse are faint; no words were marked [?].
